guide.title: Korean BBQ in Chicago's North Suburbs: Niles, Morton Grove, Glenview and Northbrook
guide.intro: Four incorporated municipalities north and north-west of Chicago — Niles, Morton Grove, Glenview and Northbrook — hold eight Korean barbecue rooms where the meat is cooked at the table on a built-in grill. Two corridors carry all eight. West Golf Road and Dempster Street run through Niles into Morton Grove and hold five, three of them on West Golf Road between the 8357 and 9020 blocks. Milwaukee Avenue and West Lake Avenue hold the other three, two in Glenview and one in Northbrook. The cuts run from wet-aged beef, marinated short ribs and pork belly to gopchang, daechang and makchang. BBQ Garden publishes all-you-can-eat tiers at $29.99 and $38.95, and two houses publish closing times of midnight. Village lines are load-bearing here: these four are separate municipalities from the City of Chicago and from each other.

sections.heading: West Golf Road and Dempster Street: Niles and Morton Grove
sections.body:
Five of the eight sit on two east–west roads that cross Niles and run on into Morton Grove. West Golf Road carries three within the 8357 to 9020 blocks; Dempster Street carries one at the western end in Niles and one further east in Morton Grove.

336 Korean Wet Aging BBQ House is at 8357 West Golf Road, Niles, IL 60714. Its grills are per-table units lit one at a time, and marinated short ribs and pork belly are cooked at the table with the staff assisting. Published hours are 4pm to 10:30pm Monday to Thursday, 4pm to midnight on Friday, 11:30am to midnight on Saturday and 11:30am to 10:30pm on Sunday.

Mr. Kimchi Korean AYCE BBQ is in Unit J at 8526 West Golf Road, in the same 8000s run. The house describes itself as an all-you-can-eat Korean barbecue restaurant offering meats and seafood grilled at the table, with the diner doing the cooking. Published hours are noon to 3pm and 5pm to midnight on Monday and Wednesday to Friday, noon to midnight on Saturday and noon to 11pm on Sunday; it closes on Tuesday.

BBQ Garden closes the run at 9020 West Golf Road. Diners grill their own meat at the table across two all-you-can-eat tiers, $29.99 and $38.95, the higher tier adding short ribs and beef tongue; there is a self-serve banchan bar and bell-call service. Published hours are 11:30am to 10pm Sunday to Tuesday and on Thursday, and 11:30am to 11pm on Friday and Saturday; it closes on Wednesday.

Dempster Street holds the other two. Jin Soo Korean BBQ is at 8788 West Dempster Street, Niles, where the meat is cooked at the table on the grill and the staff explain how to handle each cut, sometimes taking the tongs over during quieter hours. Published hours are 11:30am to 2:30pm and 4:30pm to 9:30pm Monday to Saturday, and 3pm to 9:30pm on Sunday. Dempster Street continues east over the village line, and Hwang Soh Grill is at 5819 Dempster Street, Morton Grove, working gopchang, daechang and makchang, with the cuts grilled at the table. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

sections.heading: Milwaukee Avenue and West Lake Avenue: Glenview and Northbrook
sections.body:
The other three stand north-west of the Golf Road corridor, two of them on Milwaukee Avenue as it runs out of Glenview into Northbrook, and one on West Lake Avenue in Glenview.

Gopchang Story Korean BBQ occupies Suite 201 at 1735 Milwaukee Avenue, Glenview, IL 60025. Its table grill is a flat, heat-resistant surface rather than the usual bulky barbecue pan, and gopchang, daechang and makchang are cooked on it. Published hours are 11am to 10pm Monday to Thursday and 11am to 11pm Friday to Sunday, which covers all seven days.

Pro Samgyubsal is further north on the same road, at 3420 Milwaukee Avenue, Northbrook, IL 60062 — a Northbrook address, not a Glenview one. It is a samgyeopsal house, samgyeopsal being grilled pork belly, and the diner does the grilling at the table. Published hours are 4pm to 10:45pm Monday to Saturday and 4pm to 9:45pm on Sunday.

Iron Age Korean Steakhouse is at 4513 West Lake Avenue, Glenview. The operator describes a full do-it-yourself Korean barbecue in which guests take control of the cooking at the table grill rather than the servers, and its locations page lists two Illinois rooms, this one on telephone 847-813-6029 and one at 1265 North Milwaukee Avenue in Chicago's Wicker Park. No source states the Glenview room's opening hours, so none are given here.

faq.question: What is tabletop Korean BBQ, and what counts as one?
faq.answer: Tabletop Korean barbecue means the grill is part of the dining table: a gas, charcoal or smokeless unit set into the tabletop, over which the diner cooks raw meat that arrives uncooked. Eight rooms in Niles, Morton Grove, Glenview and Northbrook work that way. A kitchen that grills the meat and carries it out is a different thing, and so are the Korean rooms nearby that serve soondubu, soups and stews, or fried chicken, none of which put a grill in front of the diner. The distinction is mechanical rather than a matter of taste: either the table has a grill in it or it does not.

faq.question: Where are they, and how are they grouped?
faq.answer: Two corridors. West Golf Road in Niles carries three between the 8357 and 9020 blocks: 336 Korean Wet Aging BBQ House at 8357, Mr. Kimchi at 8526 Unit J and BBQ Garden at 9020. Dempster Street carries two, Jin Soo at 8788 West Dempster Street in Niles and Hwang Soh Grill at 5819 Dempster Street in Morton Grove. Milwaukee Avenue carries two more, Gopchang Story at 1735 in Glenview and Pro Samgyubsal at 3420 in Northbrook, and Iron Age Korean Steakhouse stands at 4513 West Lake Avenue in Glenview.

faq.question: Which of them are all-you-can-eat, and what does it cost?
faq.answer: BBQ Garden, 9020 West Golf Road, Niles, publishes two tiers, $29.99 and $38.95, with the higher tier adding short ribs and beef tongue, plus a self-serve banchan bar and bell-call service. Mr. Kimchi Korean AYCE BBQ, 8526 West Golf Road Unit J, describes itself as an all-you-can-eat Korean barbecue restaurant offering meats and seafood grilled at the table, and publishes no price. The remaining six publish neither an all-you-can-eat format nor a per-head figure.

faq.question: Which ones close on a weekday, and how late do the rest serve?
faq.answer: Mr. Kimchi closes on Tuesday and BBQ Garden closes on Wednesday. Two houses publish closing times of midnight: 336 Korean Wet Aging BBQ House on Friday and Saturday, and Mr. Kimchi on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday. Jin Soo publishes a 9:30pm close every day, and Pro Samgyubsal 10:45pm Monday to Saturday and 9:45pm on Sunday. Gopchang Story publishes 10pm Monday to Thursday and 11pm Friday to Sunday. Hwang Soh Grill and the Glenview Iron Age publish no hours, so none are given here.

faq.question: Where do I eat gopchang, daechang and makchang?
faq.answer: Two houses name all three offal cuts. Hwang Soh Grill, 5819 Dempster Street, Morton Grove, is a gopchang, daechang and makchang specialist and grills the cuts at the table. Gopchang Story Korean BBQ, Suite 201, 1735 Milwaukee Avenue, Glenview, cooks the same three on a flat, heat-resistant table grill it uses in place of the usual bulky barbecue pan, and publishes hours across all seven days. For beef rather than offal, 336 Korean Wet Aging BBQ House works wet-aged cuts, and BBQ Garden's deluxe tier adds short ribs and beef tongue.

faq.question: Are Niles, Morton Grove, Glenview and Northbrook part of Chicago?
faq.answer: No. All four are separate incorporated municipalities in Cook County, Illinois, with their own village governments, and none of them lies inside the City of Chicago. The boundary is a municipal line rather than an editorial one, which is why Iron Age Korean Steakhouse's room at 4513 West Lake Avenue in Glenview and its room at 1265 North Milwaukee Avenue in Chicago's Wicker Park sit in different jurisdictions. Mount Prospect, Park Ridge, Chicago Ridge and North Riverside are separate municipalities again, and none of the eight rooms here is in one of them.

photos.title: Golf Mill Shopping Center on West Golf Road, Niles, Illinois
photos.description: A wide view across the surface parking lot at Golf Mill in Niles, with the centre's cylindrical office tower rising behind the low retail blocks and a run of single-storey shopfronts under a flat canopy along the right-hand side. Light traffic and parked cars fill the lot, with grass verge and mature trees in the foreground.
